outcomes: A workspace install records exact Go and Bun releases with vendor sources and per-platform SHA-256 digests
A package.json engines.node declaration neither creates a toolchain pin nor causes a Node metadata request
Refreshing toolchain metadata removes stale runtime entries that Putnami does not provision
Historical v3/v4 Node pins remain readable until that explicit refresh
A toolchain pin survives the refresh while a declared extension's runtime resolves it, even in a workspace with no project of that language
A workspace putnami init creates pins the toolchains it declares, so the commands init prints next resolve them
A checkout whose lock lacks a pin for a declared toolchain gets it from the first command's implicit install, and keeps every committed pin
A Go project created on a host with only Putnami installed is set up with the Go the lock pins, pinned and installed first when the host has none
A new Go project requires the Go framework release the consumer's module proxies serve, and create fails before it writes anything when none answers
A machine that pinned a Go release pins it again in any workspace with no request to go.dev
nonGoals: Provisioning or managing a Node runtime
Removing the TypeScript compiler's Node-compatible output target
Changing the lock format version or its compatibility window

requirements.text: Toolchain refresh derives entries only from go.work and package.json#packageManager when it names Bun. It ignores package.json#engines.node, contacts no Node release endpoint, and replaces the toolchain map so a stale Node entry no declared extension resolves cannot survive. Historical v3/v4 Node pins remain readable before that refresh.
Every generated Go or Bun toolchain entry carries an exact version, its vendor release source, and at least one vendor-published SHA-256 digest keyed by os/arch.

When no go.work or package.json declaration derives a toolchain, the refresh keeps the committed pin verbatim while a declared extension's runtime resolves its lock identity: through a task, runToolchains, or the prepare step of a local source. It makes no metadata request for it. Once no declared extension resolves it, the refresh drops the pin.

putnami init ends with the toolchain refresh putnami install ends with, after its last dependency install, so the lock pins what the new workspace declares before the commands init prints next run. A failed refresh fails init and names putnami install.

The first-use install a command runs implicitly pins each toolchain go.work or package.json#packageManager declares that the lock does not pin yet, with the same verified release metadata. It keeps every other entry as committed, stamps no CLI protocol, and creates no lock. Without a missing pin it reads no release metadata and writes nothing.

putnami projects create sets a Go project up with the go command the template extension's tasks resolve: the release the lock pins, else a go on PATH. On a host with neither, it writes a missing go.work from the project's go directive, pins the Go that go.work declares, runs workspace-install and resolves again. If no go results, it fails naming the reasons and the create command to run again with --force.

When the workspace-install that putnami projects create runs to install a missing Go fails but still leaves a go, create finishes the Go setup with that go and runs the installers no second time. It keeps the project files and the workspace membership, and exits non-zero naming putnami deps install, as putnami init --project does after a failed install.

When go mod tidy fails in the Go project putnami projects create sets up, create keeps the project files and the workspace membership and exits non-zero. The error names tidy, quotes the end of go's output with URL credentials redacted, and names the create command to run again with --force.

putnami projects create asks the proxies of the effective GOPROXY, read from the environment then the go env file, for the @latest go.putnami.dev/app version a template renders; a 404 or 410 passes to the next. direct, and a module GONOPROXY or GOPRIVATE matches, follow the origin's go-import mod tag. Requests carry the credentials go would send, never printed. When nothing answers a canonical version, create writes nothing and fails naming each source asked, the fix and the command to rerun.

An explicit putnami install pins each toolchain go.work or package.json#packageManager declares, at the declared release, when the lock pins none or another release, before any workspace installer runs, so the installers install the release the lock pins. A failed pin stops the install before the installers run. The implicit first-use install still only fills a missing pin.

putnami deps add and deps remove run go get and go mod tidy with the go command the Go extension's tasks resolve: the release the lock pins, else a go on PATH. On a host with neither, they pin and install the Go the lock pins the way projects create does, and fail naming putnami install when no go results.

When the workspace-install that putnami deps add, deps remove or deps prune runs to install a missing Go fails but still leaves a go, the command edits the Go modules with that go, and prune edits every module it selected. It runs the installers no second time and exits non-zero naming putnami deps install, as putnami projects create does, so a failed install never ends in success.

A Go pin takes the entry go.dev published for the release from a record under the Putnami home, toolchains/go/go-<version>.pin.json, and makes no request. It asks the release index only without a record that names the version and the go.dev source and maps only supported platforms to SHA-256 digests. It then writes the fetched entry as the record through a rename; a write that fails does not fail the pin. The lock holds the same bytes from the record and from the index.
